comments.text:
ACTUALLY, Walmart keeps track of "customers" via credit and debit cards. There is an increase in businesses refusing to accept CASH, and demanding credit or debit payments. There are 3 MAIN reasons...1) They can charge fees for using those methods, that range in percentage. Most Credit card companies make businesses pay a 1% to 3% fee. Businesses make customers pay that OR will charge a "flat fee" that is often higher than the fee. 2) They use the Credit/Debit cards to track customers purchases, credit history, purchasing ability, returns history, etc. (I had to return something to Walmart and brought the wrong receipt. They LITERALLY scanned my debit card and traced the purchase I made.) AND finally, 3) Cash is concrete. Someone paying with cash is MUCH LESS LIKELY to "impulse buy." Keeping cash, on hand in stores, requires bank runs, deposits, employee theft easier, robbery a higher likelihood,  etc. 

Society has been moving toward a "cashless" society for a long time. Think about what that can allow. If ALL TRANSACTIONS are digital, your life LITERALLY balances on a keystroke. Whether you have a job, a home, assests, subscriptions...ANYTHING.
